title: Hospital Beds
service: Hospital beds for home use (including variable height and electric adjustment features)

criteria.text: Condition requires body positioning not feasible in an ordinary bed
criteria.span: The patient's condition requires positioning of the body; e.g., to alleviate pain, promote good body alignment, prevent contractures, avoid respiratory infections, in ways not feasible in an ordinary bed

criteria.text: Or condition requires special attachments that cannot be used on an ordinary bed
criteria.span: The patient's condition requires special attachments that cannot be fixed and used on an ordinary bed.

criteria.text: Physician's prescription accompanies the initial claim
criteria.span: The physician's prescription, which must accompany the initial claim

criteria.text: Positioning: prescription/documentation describes the condition and the severity and frequency of symptoms
criteria.span: the prescription or other documentation must describe the medical condition, e.g., cardiac disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, quadriplegia or paraplegia, and also the severity and frequency of the symptoms of the condition that necessitates a hospital bed for positioning.

criteria.text: Attachments: prescription describes the condition and specifies the attachments
criteria.span: the prescription must describe the patient's condition and specify the attachments that require a hospital bed.

criteria.text: Variable height only for listed conditions where it assists ambulation, avoids strain getting up/down, or aids transfers
criteria.span: The condition requires the variable height feature to assist the patient to ambulate by enabling the patient to place his or her feet on the floor while sitting on the edge of the bed

criteria.text: Electric adjustments: frequent and/or immediate need for position change
criteria.span: the patient's condition requires frequent change in body position and/or there may be an immediate need for a change in body position (i.e., no delay can be tolerated)

criteria.text: Electric adjustments: patient can operate the controls (exceptions only for SCI and brain damage)
criteria.span: the patient can operate the controls and cause the adjustments. Exceptions may be made to this last requirement in cases of spinal cord injury and brain damaged patients.

notes: Much of this NCD is MAC discretion ('MAC medical staff may determine', 'Exceptions may be made'). Cases avoid discretionary branches: no case relies on the SCI/brain-damage exception to the operate-the-controls requirement, and the only variable-height case is one matching none of the listed conditions. When a case requests only a feature (electric adjustments, variable height) for a patient who already has a covered bed, the decision refers to that feature.
